home.name: Francis Desjardins
home.enough: A dependency is easy to add and hard to remove, and most of what one does goes unused. The cost of adding one never arrives on the day you add it.

skills.title: What I build
skills.description: So these three carry none. Framework-free cores with thin bindings over them: the core is plain TypeScript that runs in a browser, a worker or a service, and the binding is the only part that knows which — a test walks the import graph and fails if the core ever reaches a framework.
skills.thinking: The habit is one question asked earlier than usual: how much of this library am I actually using? A state layer that needed a set of listeners and a shallow compare was carrying two libraries to get them — nine kilobytes of published bundle, for nothing a caller could see. It stops where the library is the hard part: time zones, cryptography, anything whose difficulty is the part you have not met yet.
skills.secondary: Also: a self-declared cat person. No further questions.

work.title: What's running
work.description: Three pieces, each with a surface you can try. The names come from the shadows an eclipse casts. What they refuse to do is documented as carefully as the rest.

dialog.name: antumbra
dialog.description: Dialog manager on the native top layer. Zero shipped UI: the renderer stays yours. React, Solid and vanilla bindings.

boot.name: umbra
boot.description: Bootstrap orchestration, and not a front-end kind: the core needs no DOM, so one declared graph boots a page, a worker or a service. You say what each step needs; the parallelism is derived from that — no flag, no concurrency ceiling.

designSystem.name: penumbra
designSystem.description: The design system all three playgrounds wear — and the page that takes it apart, one layer at a time.
